title: Clo Livesync Pour Unreal Engine
description:
Dans ce workshop CLO, vous aurez une présentation rapide sur la procédure à suivre pour intégrer les vêtements CLO dans Unreal Engine en utilisant le plugin CLO LiveSync :

Qu'est-ce que Unreal Engine ?
Comment utiliser CLO LiveSync - Workflow
Créer un environnement basique sur Unreal Engine
MetaHuman dans CLO – Workflow

Souhaitez-vous nous donner votre avis sur ce Skill up ? Remplissez le formulaire ici : https://forms.gle/frs6zj7StAfy99Jh9

Traditional rendering engines take a while to generate realistic photos You will be able to realize that on CLO, for example, the rendering takes a little time to generate an image Unreal Engine does the rendering in real time The Lumens software allows you to create photorealistic visuals in real time The calculation of global lighting as well as ray tracing are included in the image creation As you can imagine, this will radically speed up the animation creation time And allow you to better express the details and movements of your creations In addition, it is extremely easy to create environments in Unreal Engine Unreal Engine includes a huge library called Quixel that we will see together Which contains 3D scanned assets of very high quality But also systems to simulate different types of water, an atmosphere, an animated sky The field of creative possibilities is largely reclaimed In order to have human characters at the same level of realism Epic has launched its MetaHuman platform MetaHuman allows you to create in a few clicks human avatars photorealistic We will see that too in the different tutorials today So, the LiveSync of CLO and Unreal, why use it? markdown_content: ## Introduction to CLO LiveSync Plugin for Unreal Engine 5 This section introduces the CLO LiveSync plugin designed for Unreal Engine 5, explaining its relevance to 3D visualization, especially in fashion, and the advantages of using Unreal Engine 5 for real-time rendering and animation. Unreal Engine, developed by Epic Games since 1998, is a leading 3D software widely used beyond game development, including automotive design, VFX, AR, and fashion. The release of Unreal Engine 5 in April 2022 introduced significant real-time rendering improvements such as the Lumen global illumination system and advanced ray tracing, enabling photorealistic visuals instantly. Unlike traditional rendering engines, Unreal Engine renders scenes in real time, dramatically accelerating animation workflows and enhancing visual fidelity. The CLO LiveSync plugin is a collaborative development between CLO and Epic Games that facilitates seamless interoperability between CLO 3D and Unreal Engine 5.3 or higher. It enables direct transfer of garments, avatars, and animations from CLO to Unreal without laborious manual exports in formats like FBX or OBJ. The plugin preserves texture quality, material properties, and physical simulation data, significantly streamlining the pipeline for fashion visualization in Unreal Engine. --- ## Installing and Setting Up the CLO LiveSync Plugin in Unreal Engine 5.3+ This section covers the installation requirements and initial setup steps for the CLO LiveSync plugin and its dependencies, including configuring Unreal Engine settings for optimal stability and functionality. - **Plugin Download and Installation:** - The LiveSync plugin is available on the CLO Connect website under the Apps category. - After downloading, unzip the plugin folder. - Copy and paste the plugin files into the Unreal Engine directory: `Engine/Plugins/Marketplace`. - The plugin requires Unreal Engine version 5.3 or newer; earlier versions are not supported. - **Substance Plugin Requirement:** - For correct shader functionality, the Substance 3D plugin must be installed in Unreal Engine 5.3+. - Install it via the Epic Games Launcher Marketplace by searching for "Substance 3D for Unreal Engine" and downloading it. - **Enabling Plugins in Unreal Engine:** - Open Unreal Engine and navigate to `Settings > Plugins`. - Verify that both the CLO LiveSync and Substance plugins are activated (locked). - Restart Unreal Engine after activation to apply changes. - **Adjusting Unreal Engine Settings:** - Change the Rendering Hardware Interface (RHI) from DirectX 12 to DirectX 11 to reduce crashes and freezes. - Enable **Order Independent Transparency** under the Translucency settings to properly render fabric transparency effects. - After applying these settings, restart Unreal Engine to finalize the setup. --- ## Creating and Preparing a Project for CLO LiveSync This section details how to create a new Unreal Engine project suitable for CLO LiveSync and optimize CLO projects before import. - **Starting a Project:** - Launch Unreal Engine and create a new project, preferably starting from a preset like "Automotive Product Design Blank" for simplicity. - Project naming convention: Avoid spaces; use underscores, dashes, or slashes. - Save the project in an appropriate directory and wait for Unreal Engine to initialize the project. - **Preparing CLO Project for Import:** - Optimize overpictures by converting OBJ-type overpictures to texture-based overpictures to reduce polygon count and stitching complexity. - Convert mesh topology from triangles to quads in CLO’s property editor to reduce polygon counts without significantly affecting fabric drapery quality. - Save optimized CLO projects before importing. --- ## Using the CLO LiveSync Plugin Interface and Import Workflow This section explains how to use the LiveSync plugin interface within Unreal Engine and the workflow for importing CLO garments and avatars. - **Opening the Plugin:** - Access LiveSync via the Unreal Engine `Windows` menu at the bottom. - The plugin interface includes a 3D viewport and two adjustable side columns. - CLO must remain open in the background during synchronization. - **Importing Garments:** - Click the plugin icon in the top-left corner. - Disable CLO simulation mode during export to avoid background animation calculations. - Confirm export; an update progress bar appears. - Import time depends on garment complexity, particle distance settings, PC performance, and texture quality. - Imported garments appear gradually in the viewport. - **Navigation Controls in Plugin Viewport:** - Select garment and press `F` to frame. - Hold `Alt` + left-click to orbit. - Hold `Alt` + right-click to zoom. - Mouse wheel click enables panning. - **Import Options:** - Clothes can be recorded as Static Mesh (geometry only) or Geometry Cache (geometry + animation). - Avatars can be recorded as Static Mesh or Skeletal Mesh (includes rig for animation). - Body animations can be applied directly to skeletal mesh avatars within Unreal Engine. --- ## Managing Imported CLO Assets and Material Adjustments This section describes how to organize imported CLO assets within Unreal Engine and adjust materials for improved realism. - **Saving Geometry Cache:** - After import, save geometry cache files in the Unreal project’s Content folder for organization. - Name files logically for easy retrieval. - **Adding Garments to Scene:** - Drag and drop saved geometry cache assets from Content Drawer into the scene. - Automatic material assignment occurs during import, preserving fabric details like transparency, metallic effects, and folds. - **Material Instances:** - Materials are imported as simplified material instances rather than complex node trees, easing modification. - Adjust normal map intensity to enhance surface detail, e.g., increasing the glossiness or roughness effects on leather or metallic fabrics. - Colors can be changed directly in Unreal Engine to create colorway iterations or animations without re-exporting from CLO. --- ## Creating Environments Using Quixel Megascans in Unreal Engine This section introduces environment creation with Quixel Megascans integration in Unreal Engine for realistic scenes. - **Accessing Quixel Content:** - Open the Content Drawer and click “Add Quixel Content.” - Log in with the same Epic Games account used for Unreal Engine and MetaHuman to unify asset management. - Quixel library contains over 13,000 high-quality scanned 3D models and materials. - **Downloading and Adding Assets:** - Search for assets (e.g., “Stone”) and select quality levels based on project needs. - Download assets and add them to the project content. - Drag static mesh assets into the scene to populate the environment. - **Using Gizmo for Object Manipulation:** - Use the spacebar to switch between translation, rotation, and scale gizmos. - Duplicate objects by holding `Alt` and dragging to create variations in the scene. - Use mirror transforms to break repetition and increase realism. - **Foliage Tool for Vegetation:** - Switch to Foliage mode to paint plants, grass, and trees naturally. - Select static meshes from a Megascan subfolder (e.g., 3D Plants). - Configure brush size, density, scale variation, and paint foliage across the terrain. - Adjust parameters to simulate natural plant size and distribution variation. --- ## Using MetaHuman for Realistic Human Avatars This section outlines creating, importing, and animating photorealistic humanoid avatars with Epic’s MetaHuman platform integrated into Unreal Engine. - **MetaHuman Overview:** - MetaHuman is a cloud-based avatar creation platform accessed via an Epic Games account. - It allows rapid generation and customization of high-fidelity human avatars. - Clothing should be removed in MetaHuman Creator to avoid conflicts with CLO garments. - **Importing MetaHumans into Unreal:** - MetaHumans are saved in your Quixel Bridge account. - Import MetaHuman assets via Quixel Bridge in Unreal Engine. - Place the avatar at origin coordinates (0,0,0) for consistent positioning. - **Creating Animation Sequences:** - Create a new Level Sequence in Unreal Engine. - Add the MetaHuman actor to the sequencer. - Use the Control Rig to pose and animate the avatar by setting keyframes. - Export animation sequences for further processing. - **Exporting and Synchronizing with CLO:** - Export animation sequences as Skeletal Meshes. - In CLO, start a new project and import the MetaHuman skeleton mesh via LiveSync. - CLO receives the physical structure without textures for garment creation. - Apply CLO garments and simulate fabric on the avatar. --- ## Rig Retargeting and Animation Application This section describes how to retarget animations from Unreal Engine default avatars to MetaHumans and apply animations to garments. - **IK Retargeter Setup:** - Use Unreal Engine’s IK Retargeter to transfer animations between different rigs. - Add the Epic-provided Third Person Pack for sample avatars and animations. - Set the source rig and mesh (e.g., IK Mannequin) and the target rig (MetaHuman). - Adjust mesh offsets for side-by-side comparison. - **Applying Animations:** - Select an animation (e.g., Idle) from the source avatar. - Export the retargeted animation sequence to your MetaHuman folder. - Apply the animation sequence to the MetaHuman actor by changing animation mode to Custom Asset. - **Animating CLO Garments:** - Export the animated MetaHuman skeletal mesh back to CLO via LiveSync. -
